answer: Never let an identity grade its own kin. When an agent's work needs approval, the system draws a jury at random from unrelated clusters: no shared owner, no common funding trail, no history of mutual attestation, like a harbor master who refuses to let ships from the same fleet inspect each other. Fraud cannot hide in a quiet lagoon of friendly graders; each fake must fool strangers who gain nothing from approving it. To an attacker the cost is steep: one fake means planting accomplices across many independent groups, and one honest dissent sends a ripple of re-checks through the batch.
